stories.summary: Mozambique: nouvelle saisie d'une importante quantité de fentanyl à l'aéroport de Maputo Les autorités mozambicaines ont découvert 1,4 tonne de fentanyl dissimulé entre des flacons de cosmétiques en provenance du Brésil, jeudi 13 août. stories.summary: La Turquie se positionne en Libye et veut apparaître comme une puissance réconciliatrice Avant de faire le déplacement en Égypte ce jeudi 13 août, le chef de la diplomatie turque Hakan Fidan a effectué une visite de deux jours en Libye où il a rencontré les responsables de deux camps libyens en visitant à la fois Tripoli et Benghazi. stories.summary: Nigeria: 2027 - Tinubu Urged to Back Tompolo for Grassroots Mobilisation 14 August 2026 Vanguard (Lagos) By Joseph Erunke, Abuja A Niger Delta stakeholder, Chief Ebi Nelson, has urged President Bola Ahmed Tinubu to recognise and strengthen the role of Chief Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, in the mobilisation of grassroots support for the President's 2027 re-election bid. stories.summary: Malawi: Police Commissioner Accused of Sexually Exploiting 45 Female Officers Forced Into Retirement 14 August 2026 Nyasa Times (Leeds) By Nyasa Times Reporter A senior Malawi Police commissioner has been forced into retirement after being found guilty of sexually exploiting dozens of female officers under his command, sparking outrage from human rights campaigners who say the punishment falls dangerously short of justice. Stan Kaliza, who oversaw human resources, management and development for the Malawi Police Service, has been sent on forced retirement, following a disciplinary process that ended in disgrace for the once-powerful officer. Brian Ng'oma, Director of Operations at the Police Service Commission, confirmed that Kaliza had been found guilty on nine separate charges -- though he remained tight-lipped when pressed for further details on the specific nature of each charge or the evidence presented during the disciplinary hearing. At the heart of the scandal are allegations that Kaliza sexually exploited 45 female police officers during the course of his career, with the Malawi Police Service Commission ultimately upholding the accusations after an internal investigation and disciplinary hearing. stories.title: Malawi: Roads Blocked, Tempers Boil - - Kabaza Crackdown Turns Ugly
stories.summary: Malawi: Roads Blocked, Tempers Boil - - Kabaza Crackdown Turns Ugly 14 August 2026 Nyasa Times (Leeds) By Nyasa Times Reporter Malawi's long-running Kabaza crisis has exploded into fresh confrontation, with police, councils and Kabaza associations rolling out tough new enforcement measures -- and riders responding with roadblocks, protests and fury. The latest clashes unfolded in Limbe, Blantyre, where Kabaza operators blocked roads during a joint operation by police and the Malawi Coalition of Kabaza Associations (Macoaka). Officers impounded motorcycles, demanded registration, and pushed riders out of central business districts -- prompting angry scenes as operators accused authorities of "harsh" tactics. But Macoaka chairperson Moses Mwalabu was blunt: "They were given enough time." He insists riders have ignored repeated warnings to register their bikes, undergo training and comply with basic safety rules. The crackdown comes as Malawi faces a deadly Kabaza epidemic.

The court said the respondents' decision to simply "abide" by the High Court's decision meant critical arguments and information were never placed before the court. Justice Ben Hlatshwayo, writing for the unanimous court, said the respondents' conduct was unacceptable in a case involving fundamental rights, children and reproductive health. stories.title: Presidential pardon for French alleged spy accused of plotting Mali coup
stories.summary: Image source, AFP via Getty Images Image caption, President Assimi GoÃ¯ta (pictured) has pardoned French national Yann Vezilier By Natasha Booty Â and Â Wycliffe Muia Published 13 August 2026 A Frenchman who was sentenced to 20 years in prison in Mali for plotting an alleged coup in the West African country has now been granted a presidential pardon, it was announced on Thursday. Yann Vezilier was accused a year ago of trying to destabilise President Assimi GoÃ¯ta's government "on behalf of the French intelligence service" alongside a number of army generals and dozens of soldiers. It is not yet clear what has prompted Mali's U-turn. France's foreign ministry has yet to comment on the pardoning, and previously said accusations that Vezilier was working in Mali as a French spy were "unfounded". In a post on Facebook , external , the Malian government said: "This act of clemency, which does not call into question the facts established by an adversarial judgment rendered during a trial, where all rights of the defence were respected, is accompanied by the immediate removal of the individual from national territory." Mali is a former colony of France, and has been gripped by a security crisis fuelled by an Islamist insurgency since 2012.

stories.title: Ebola en RDC: derrière les millions annoncés pour la riposte, le défi de coordonner les financements
stories.summary: Ebola en RDC: derrière les millions annoncés pour la riposte, le défi de coordonner les financements En République démocratique du Congo (RDC), le coût prévu de la riposte à Ebola change fortement d’échelle. Prévu pour une durée de trois mois, le premier plan national avait été budgété à 240 millions de dollars. Non finalisé encore, le nouveau plan présenté par le gouvernement qui doit financer non seulement la lutte contre le virus, mais aussi la continuité des services essentiels de santé, atteint, lui, désormais, 940 millions de dollars, selon Anne Ancia, représentante de l’OMS en RDC. Dans le même temps, plusieurs bailleurs internationaux annoncent des centaines de millions de dollars qui ne passent pas tous par les mêmes circuits. stories.title: DRC’s fast-growing Ebola outbreak spreads to sixth province
stories.summary: People in protective clothing lower the coffin of an Ebola victim into a grave in Bunia, Ituri province, on Tuesday. Photograph: Dieudonne Dirole/AP DRC’s fast-growing Ebola outbreak spreads to sixth province Man dies in Bas-Uele after travelling from Haut-Uele, as head of WHO says outbreak on track to be deadliest ever The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has spread to a sixth province, officials have said, a day after the head of the World Health Organization said the outbreak was on track to surpass the deadliest in history, which killed at least 11,000 people more than a decade ago. stories.title: French ambassador to CAR investigated over claims he hosted dozens of women

The investigation comes as Paris seeks to rebuild relations with CAR after their sharp deterioration in recent years amid Russia’s expanding influence in the former French colony. stories.title: Tanzanian rangers arrested as police investigate death in national park
stories.summary: Image source, Getty Images Image caption, The Ngongoro Conservation Area is a protected zone By Alfred Lasteck BBC Africa ,Â Reporting from Dar es Salaam Published 13 August 2026 Tanzania's police have arrested three park rangers after a man died and two others were injured in a conservation area which they were accused of entering illegally. The three men had been detained by rangers on Wednesday morning in the protected Ngorongoro Conservation Area, where rights groups have long raised concerns about alleged human rights violations linked to conservation enforcement. They were arrested after they were accused of entering the area on a motorcycle without following required procedures. Police said the men had been travelling from the northern city of Arusha towards Babati, about 166km (103 miles) away, to attend a funeral when they lost their way. Police are investigating the circumstances in which Sefu Musa, 25, later died.

stories.title: Eritrea, a rising power along a global shipping artery
stories.summary: https://p.dw.com/p/5Igaq Eritrea's location at the Bab Al-Mandeb Strait is an asset for the autocratic nation, as partner from near and far seek access to the Red Sea Image: ABACA/picture alliance Advertisement Across the Horn of Africa , geopolitical interests of various countries continue to cause tensions and conflict as part of the growing competition for political influence over the region. In its own right, the small country of Eritrea appears to be gaining in importance within this context: The autocratic state run by long-standing ruler Isaias Afwerki controls strategically important coastal points on the Red Sea, especially with its ports of Assab and Massawa. In July, a series of diplomatic consultations in Cairo involving regional powers like Egypt, Somalia , Eritrea, and a high-ranking US envoy highlighted Eritrea's growing role in helping to coordinate approaches to resolving serious security challenges in the Horn of Africa and the Red Sea, and to facilitate trade. Eritrea's unique location along this maritime route is notably becoming more and more strategic in light of international trade conflicts. The small nation's coastline near the Bab-al-Mandab Strait stretches for more than 1,000 kilometers (621.4 miles), bordering Sudan to the northwest and Djibouti to the southeast.

stories.title: Africa: The US-China Rivalry Is Gradually Shaping Pan-African Mining Dynamics
stories.summary: The US-China Rivalry Is Gradually Shaping Pan-African Mining Dynamics 13 August 2026 Content from a Premium Partner InfoWire The global energy transition and the quest for critical minerals required to develop the new technologies and industries associated with this dynamic have contributed to Africa becoming one of the world's most coveted mining investment destinations. China, the continent's largest foreign mine operator, and the US have been the most active in this regard, with their ongoing mining investment push supporting the development of concessions, railways, energy infrastructure, and other major projects. Nevertheless, there are concerns that this ongoing mineral push will subject African countries to the superpower rivalry between Beijing and Washington, with the US highlighting that its increased engagement in Africa is motivated by its intention to reduce Beijing's continental mineral dominance. Against this backdrop, there are allegations, notably from Zambia, that the US has conditioned the signing of bilateral health partnership agreements on ensuring access to US critical minerals. In parallel, despite being the continent's largest international mining investor, Chinese companies have been accused, including by labour unions and local media outlets, of poor worker treatment and importing Chinese labour for their projects.

stories.title: Ayra Starr on her secret relationship and teasing Stevie Wonder
stories.summary: Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Ayra Starr is a multiple Grammy and Mobo Award nominee, for hit songs like Rush, Commas, Sability and Gimme Dat By Mark Savage Music correspondent Published 13 August 2026 There's resilience, and then there's Ayra Starr. Two weeks before the release of her new album, Starrgirl, the Nigerian singer posted a photo from hospital, after undergoing "major surgery". "I was hoping it would be a quick recovery, but it was more complicated than they expected," she told fans , external , without disclosing the nature of the procedure. Within seven days, she was back in the dance studio, rehearsing for forthcoming performances with a large bandage strapped across her stomach. TV appearances, fan events and live performances followed. "I'm healing," she told the US breakfast TV show, Today. "I have strength today. I'm so happy I was able to even be here today and be able to do this." It's a display of the tenacity and ambition that's defined Starr's career to date.

stories.title: Vultures are disappearing in Nigeria - but the 'Vulture King' is fighting to reverse the trend
stories.summary: Image source, Universal Images Group via Getty Images Image caption, Some see them as sinister but these birds play a vital role in nature's cycle By Makuochi Okafor BBC Africa ,Â Reporting from Awka-Etiti, Nigeria Published 13 August 2026 "People fear the environment where the shrine is. So, nobody fights vultures that perch here," a man they call the Vulture King tells the BBC. Mostly associated with death and decay, perhaps it is not surprising that when vultures disappeared from the skies across many West African cities, they were not missed. Yet across the continent, their disappearance is becoming impossible to ignore, as conservationists warn that hunting linked to traditional beliefs and spiritual practices continues to threaten several vulture species to the point of near extinction. Without vultures, ecosystems would lose a natural defence against the spread of disease.

stories.title: Halting the march of the African armyworm: a natural cure offers hope to farmers

stories.title: Ceuta showed just how easily Europe can be divided
stories.summary: Spanish police check documents of travellers from Italy at Madrid Barajas airport, 8 August 2026, after a dispute between the two countries. Photograph: Spanish Police/Reuters View image in fullscreen Spanish police check documents of travellers from Italy at Madrid Barajas airport, 8 August 2026, after a dispute between the two countries. Photograph: Spanish Police/Reuters Ceuta showed just how easy it is to divide Europe Paul Taylor The migrant influx prompted recriminations and a tit-for-tat dispute between Italy and Spain. Putin, Erdoğan and others will have taken note W ithin hours of the first pictures of tens of thousands of migrants swimming the short distance from Morocco to the Spanish north African enclave of Ceuta hitting social media on 30 July, 22 European Union leaders , the Trump administration and Israel had piled on to criticise Madrid. The outbreak of hysteria and recrimination was a case study in 21st-century politics, driven by real-time images in a media echo chamber where populists set the agenda on migration, propagating fear, prejudice and demagogic proposals.

stories.title: Tchad: l'ex-Premier ministre et opposant Succès Masra gracié par le président Déby et libéré

stories.title: Ancestral Visions of the Future review – visceral cine-memoir is a haunting return to Lesotho

Photograph: Agat Films Review Ancestral Visions of the Future review – visceral cine-memoir is a haunting return to Lesotho Lemohang Jeremiah Mosese pairs his literary-grade voiceover with propulsive, prophetic images to interrogate his identity and that of his colonialism-carved homeland H ere is a captivating stream of consciousness film about exile, roots and identity by Lemohang Jeremiah Mosese, director of the lauded 2019 activism story This Is Not a Burial, It’s a Resurrection . It’s ostensibly a cine-memoir looking back from the vantage point of present-day Berlin to his upbringing in Lesotho, narrated by Mosese’s dense, literary-grade voiceover. stories.title: Evidence that South African special forces murdered top detective shared with BBC

stories.title: Nigeria's mass wedding - and how telling lovers from fraudsters is proving tricky
stories.summary: Image source, Getty Images Image caption, All the new wedding outfits are paid for by the Kano state government By Mansur Abubakar Reporting from Abuja Published 9 August 2026 Celebrations have turned the northern Nigerian city of Kano into a riot of colour and excitement over the last week as 1,500 couples married at a mass wedding. For days the city's streets have been buzzing with bridal parties and their families preparing outfits and attending other organised events.
